subject: NeedlePoint procurement: onboarding route & PO vs card options
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emily Barnes <emily.barnes@needlepoint.com>, procurement@needlepoint.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: NeedlePoint procurement: onboarding route & PO vs card options

Hi Emily / NeedlePoint procurement team —

Great to speak today. Quick recap from our call and the options for commercial onboarding so your AP team can pick the cleanest path: 

Summary of the ask:
- NeedlePoint needs a predictable production inference path for pilot (30k tokens/day avg) with eventual expansion.
- Procurement preference, internal vendor onboarding checklist, and timeline will determine whether a PO (net-30) or corporate card route works best.
- You asked whether purchasing via a marketplace listing (AWS/Azure) would allow immediate card payment and simplify vendor setup.

Options we can support (short list):
1) PO / Invoice (net-30) — standard vendor setup; requires W-9, signed MSA or statement of work, and vendor form.
2) Corporate card — immediate activation for card-friendly teams; single-charge limits apply (we typically see limits up to $25k without pre-approval).
3) Marketplace purchase — once live on AWS/Azure Marketplace it becomes a SaaS purchase via the marketplace billing flow (card or consolidated invoice per marketplace rules). Listing is in progress and could be enabled during the pilot window if you want us to prioritize it.

What I attached: vendor onboarding form + our redlines on the MSA (Draft_MSA_redlines.docx). I'll also attach a short SOC2 summary in my follow-up.

Next steps I propose:
- Emily / AP: confirm preferred route (PO vs card vs marketplace) and any internal vendor setup checklist items we should surface (vendor code, ERP system e.g., Coupa/Ariba, payment terms).
- If PO: please share the vendor portal URL and contact for the person who will submit the setup (we’ll return W-9 + requested docs same day).
- If card / marketplace: confirm single-transaction limits or any internal policy blockers.

Happy to align on a mutual action plan once you confirm; target timeline for pilot kick is Oct 18 if onboarding completes this week.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf (PDF), Draft_MSA_redlines.docx (DOCX)
From: Emily Barnes <emily.barnes@needlepoint.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@needlepoint.com
Date: 2027-10-03T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NeedlePoint procurement: onboarding route & PO vs card options

Karthik, Marissa —

Thanks for the summary and attachments. A few quick clarifications from AP & procurement side: 

Current constraints:
- NeedlePoint prefers PO/invoice for any new vendor > $10k ARR; our standard is net-30.
- Vendor setup lives in Coupa; procurement@needlepoint.com will need the completed vendor form + W-9 + SOC2 or security questionnaire for cloud vendors.
- We have a strict vendor onboarding timeline that typically takes 7–10 business days for standard vendors, longer if we need additional security evidence.

About marketplace: that would be ideal since it often bypasses vendor setup and allows card billing or consolidated marketplace invoicing. Do you have an ETA for when Redwood will be fully listed on AWS Marketplace (or Azure)? If it’s a few weeks, we might still prefer to proceed with a PO for the pilot to avoid blocking timelines.

Action items from our side:
- I’ll send a Coupa vendor request after we receive your completed Vendor_Onboarding_Form and W-9.
- I can expedite SOC2 review if you can send a one-page SOC2 summary or link to your audit report.

Would you be able to provide the SOC2 one-pager today? Also confirm whether Redwood will accept a signed PO + standard MSA redlines we saw in the attached DOCX.

Best,
Emily Barnes
Head of Procurement, NeedlePoint Inc.
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0128
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emily Barnes <emily.barnes@needlepoint.com>, procurement@needlepoint.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: NeedlePoint procurement: onboarding route & PO vs card options

Thanks Emily — appreciate the detail. Quick answers and a suggested path: 

1) SOC2 summary: attached (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) — one page SOC2 + link to full SOC2 report available to signed prospects under NDA.
2) Marketplace ETA: we are on track to be in AWS Marketplace in ~3 weeks; Azure timing is similar but could slip. If you want, we can flag NeedlePoint as a priority marketplace onboarding to shorten that window.
3) MSA / PO acceptance: We can accept a signed PO with our standard MSA redlines for the pilot. If you need us to sign your PO template, please have your Coupa/vendor contact upload it and we’ll return the completed vendor packet + W-9 same business day.

Interim pragmatic options so you don’t stall the pilot:
- Option A (fastest): card payment for initial pilot commits (if procurement can allow card for pilot budget).
- Option B (usual): submit Coupa vendor packet and we process net-30 invoice once vendor is added (7–10 business days).
- Option C (medium): we issue an invoice under a temporary contract for pilot (60-day term) while marketplace listing completes; Redwood can accept that for limited pilots with pre-approved finance contact.

What we will deliver today if you confirm:
- Completed Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf + W-9 (EFT details)
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (attached)
- A clean invoice template and a one-page pilot SOW to attach to the PO if you want.

Please advise preferred route and, if PO, the Coupa portal link and the person who will initiate vendor setup.

Thanks —
Karthik
Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

Subject: Re: NeedlePoint procurement: onboarding route & PO vs card options

Karthik —

Good recap. Quick internal notes / recommendation before we finalize: 
- Approve offering Option C (temporary invoice) for the pilot if AP insists on PO but timeline is tight. Limits: pilot capped at $20k without additional finance sign-off.
- I’ll ask Legal to prioritize the MSA redlines; Monica, please prep a one-page cost summary and the 60-day pilot SOW so we can attach to the PO.
- If they prefer card, flag with Customer Success to confirm funding headcount/limits.

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
